subject: theo
title: DFA → regex
description: Eliminate the states of a DFA until a regular expression is left.
promptTemplate: Create a DFA of {{level}} difficulty (easy: 2–3 states, medium: 3–4, exam: 4 with loops) to convert into a regular expression by state elimination. Do not state the elimination order. When checking: equivalence of the result matters more than its form; check each elimination step on its own.
answerFormat: Elimination steps one after another, the regular expression at the end.

drills.prompt: In state elimination you remove state q. It has a self-loop labelled r, an incoming edge p → q labelled s and an outgoing edge q → t labelled u. What is the new label on p → t (ignoring an existing direct edge)?
drills.explanation: From p you go to q (s), loop any number of times (r*), then leave to t (u).

drills.prompt: Give a regular expression for the language of this DFA.
drills.explanation: It accepts the words with an even number of a's, e.g. `b*(ab*ab*)*`.

drills.prompt: Give a regular expression for the language of this DFA.
drills.explanation: The DFA accepts exactly the words ending in ab: `(a|b)*ab`.

drills.prompt: Give a regular expression for the language of this DFA. Hint: eliminate s1 first.
drills.explanation: It accepts the words without two b's in a row, e.g. `(a|ba)*(b|ε)`.

drills.prompt: Put the steps of state elimination in order.
items: Add a new start state and a new single final state, joined with ε-edges.
Pick a state that is neither the new start nor the new final state.
Replace every path through it by a direct edge labelled in · loop* · out.
Repeat until only start and final state are left: the edge label is the expression.
